claims.claim: The strict client parser rejects a plugin manifest carrying an unknown top-level field (telemetry) and the error names the field; the strictest-supported-client requirement (rejection) and the never-emit requirement are both checked.
Both-states control: the same manifest without the unknown field is accepted by the strict parser.

Schema-diff signal: across 200 generated manifests the emitter's emitted field set is a subset of the strict accepted set, and the emitter refuses a forced foreign field at authoring time; the lenient parser (plain json.loads, no allowlist) demonstrably ACCEPTS the unknown field, proving the strict rejection is distinguishing behavior.

negative_controls.description: The known-broken lenient parser accepts the poisoned manifest, so the strict parser's rejection is a real distinguishing behavior, not a tautology.
negative_controls.good_state_output: strict parser raises StrictManifestError naming telemetry

implementation.strict_error: StrictManifestError(message, field) - message names every unknown field
implementation.emitter: emit() refuses any field outside ACCEPTED_TOP_LEVEL at authoring time

observations.name: unknown top-level field rejection
observations.method: strict parse of a poisoned manifest; error captured with .field

observations.name: emitter-to-accepted schema diff over generated manifests
observations.measured: subset holds across 200/200 generated manifests; foreign field refused at emit
observations.method: random field-subset generation + emit + strict re-parse

residual_unknowns.claim: The accepted-set pin is the probe-local closed allowlist the unit demands; a real client schema (plugin manifest spec) may pin a different field universe, in which case ACCEPTED_TOP_LEVEL is the only line to re-bind.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Re-bind ACCEPTED_TOP_LEVEL to the shipped manifest schema and re-run both probes.
